name: Kosta & Rinn Herringbone Pullover
description:
A mid-weight pullover sweater in a classic herringbone weave, cut slightly oversized with a ribbed crewneck and cuffs. The wool-analog fabric is dense enough to hold its shape through a workweek but soft enough to wear against bare skin. Available in four muted colorways: slate, bark, ash, and a deep burgundy called 'Korinthia.' The chest panel is subtly textured, giving it a handmade quality that the automated looms deliberately try to replicate.

Kosta & Rinn is a mid-tier label out of the Milwaukee corridor, family-operated for three generations, now producing out of a licensed micro-factory in Tier 3 residential. It sells in department stores and a few boutique shops. People who buy it tend to keep it for years.
what_it_says: You dress with intention without making it a statement. You probably own fewer clothes than most people but they're all good ones.
worn_by: people who grew up Tier 2 and made it to 3
story_hooks: A character finds one in their deceased parent's closet, still folded. It fits perfectly.
Kosta & Rinn is being quietly acquired by a corponation that plans to offshore production — the current run may be the last authentic batch.
Two strangers at a transit hub are wearing the same colorway and one of them takes it as a sign.
